$$
\begin{aligned}
a_i + a_j &= I_1 \in \mathbb{Z} \\
a_i + a_k &= I_2 \in \mathbb{Z}
\end{aligned}
$$
Subtracting these two equations gives:
$$
(a_i + a_j) - (a_i + a_k) = I_1 - I_2 \implies a_j - a_k = \text{Integer}
$$
This means that the difference between any two elements in the sequence must be an integer. We can fix $a_1$ and write $a_i$ as:
$$
a_i = a_1 + c_i \quad \text{where } c_i \in \mathbb{Z} \text{ and } c_1 = 0.
$$
Since $a_i$ are distinct, the integers $c_i$ must be distinct.

Now substitute this structure into the pairwise sums:
$$
a_i + a_j = (a_1 + c_i) + (a_1 + c_j) = 2a_1 + (c_i + c_j)
$$
Since $a_i + a_j$ must be an integer, and $c_i + c_j$ is an integer, it follows that $2a_1$ must be an integer. We can write $2a_1 = K$, where $K \in \mathbb{Z}$.
